claims.text: Vec garantit une performance optimale lors de l’accès séquentiel.
VecDeque réutilise la mémoire en masquant les éléments supprimés et évite ainsi les allocations fréquentes.
Vec offre un coût amorti O(1) pour push et pop à la fin.
Vec devient O(n) lors des insertions au début uniquement si la capacité doit être réallouée.
Vec est un tableau dynamique contigu dont le contenu est alloué sur le tas.
Vec a une indexation O(1), un ajout final amorti O(1) et un retrait final O(1).

quotes.P1:
A contiguous growable array type with heap-allocated contents, written Vec<T>.
Vectors have O(1) indexing, amortized O(1) push (to the end) and O(1) pop (from the end).
When the type is non-zero-sized and the capacity is nonzero, Vec uses the Global allocator for its allocation. It is valid to convert both ways between such a Vec and a raw pointer allocated with the Global allocator, provided that the Layout used with the allocator is correct for a sequence of capacity elements of the type, and the first len values pointed to by the raw pointer are valid. More precisely, a ptr: *mut T that has been allocated with the Global allocator with Layout::array::<T>(capacity) may be converted into a vec using Vec::<T>::from_raw_parts(ptr, len, capacity). Conversely, the memory backing a value: *mut T obtained from Vec::<T>::as_mut_ptr may be deallocated using the Global allocator with the same layout.
quotes.P2:
A double-ended queue (deque) implemented with a growable ring buffer.
This queue has O(1) amortized inserts and removals from both ends of the container. It also has O(1) indexing like a vector. The contained elements are not required to be copyable, and the queue will be sendable if the contained type is sendable.
quotes.P3:
Sequences: Vec, VecDeque, LinkedList
§Use a VecDeque when:
Throughout the documentation, we will adhere to the following conventions for operation notation:
Operations which have an amortized cost are suffixed with a *.
Calling operations that add to a collection will occasionally require a collection to be resized - an extra operation that takes O(n) time.
Rust’s collections never automatically shrink, so removal operations aren’t amortized.
| | get(i) | insert(i) | remove(i) | append(Vec(m)) | split_off(i) | range | append
| Vec | O(1) | O(n-i)* | O(n-i) | O(m)* | O(n-i) | N/A | N/A
| VecDeque | O(1) | O(min(i, n-i))* | O(min(i, n-i)) | O(m)* | O(min(i, n-i)) | N/A | N/A
Note that where ties occur, Vec is generally going to be faster than VecDeque, and VecDeque is generally going to be faster than LinkedList.
